items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Cy Touf was playing second trombone... I played first trombone... And that first night Woody calls up “Four Others.”... So I did this thing... So then I was on Woody’s band

ctx.x: Cy Touf was playing second trombone, I mean but he played the bass trumpet, and he wasn’t strong enough sound-wise to play lead, and Bobby Lamb was playing third trombone, who is a very good trombone player but he was kind of green then. I think he was kind of green then. He was a very good trombone player. He’s matured. I don’t know if you know the name, Bobby Lamb. He’s a very good trombone player that lives in England. But Bobby would get so drunk that the cops couldn’t understand him when they’d pick him up…

reading I’ve ever witnessed,” he says, “that was terrific.” And I said, “Well I wasn’t sight reading, Woody,” I said, “I’d heard that record so many times that I knew what was coming.” You know I’d heard and listened to the record. When you know what’s coming you’re not really reading. So then I was on Woody’s band through pretty much up until June or July of ’56. And somewhere around March or April Bill Harris came back to the band. And he came back to the band playing second trombone. I guess he was just…
